chunks: One of our companions, from Abu Jareer Al-Qummi, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'We buy hawks and enter them into the Haram, so is that permissible for us?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Everything from the birds that enters the Haram, from those that array their wings, has entered into its safety, so free its way.'

key_terms.مَأْمَنَهُ: Its safety/protection (status of being safe from harm)
key_terms.يَصُفُّ جَنَاحَهُ: Arrays/displays its wings (indicating readiness or presence)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on bringing hawks into the Haram and hunting birds there?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of 'ma'man' (sanctuary) for birds of prey entering the Haram, establishing their protection from hunting based on the physical act of displaying their wings. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the sanctity of the Haram extends to its fauna, granting them a temporary status of inviolability once they enter the sacred boundary. This ruling underscores the broader Islamic emphasis on preserving wildlife within holy sites as a manifestation of divine mercy.

en.hubeali: One of our companions, from Abu Jareer Al Qummy who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘We bought hawks and we entered the Al-Harram. So is that for us?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Everything from the birds which enters the Al-Harram, from what arrays its wings, so it has entered into its safety, therefore, free its way’.
en.sarwar: 19. Certain persons of our people have narrated from abu Jarir al-Qummiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of our buying hawks and taking them to al-Haram (the sacred area), if we owe anything. He (the Imam) said, ‘If one takes any of the birds that when flying, flap their wing, he has taken them to their sanctuary, and should leave them there.’”
